network.overall_strategy: Experimentally grounded synthesis is anchored on the surface cyanosulfidic sequence of Patel et al. (2015), in which 3-aminopropanal is converted to rac-proline by cyanohydrin formation, H2S-driven thiolation-cyclization, Cu0/H2S reductive deoxygenation, thione-to-nitrile exchange, and nitrile hydrolysis. The network therefore focuses on surface chemistry and supplies 3-aminopropanal through three chemically plausible feeder channels: direct acrolein amination, glycerol dehydration followed by amination, or net reductive amination of malondialdehyde. Because the validated chemistry is racemic rather than asymmetric, the requested L-proline target is interpreted as an L-enriched pool reached by explicitly speculative post-synthetic enrichment at biochemical mineral interfaces or by asymmetric crystallization. High-temperature hydrothermal routes are not emphasized because the key amino aldehyde and aminonitrile intermediates are better supported and likely more persistent in milder surface pools. Ten representative pathways are enumerated from these branches.

reactions.name: Glycerol dehydration to acrolein

conditions.other: drying films at volcanic hot spring or subaerial geothermal margins

reactions.mechanism: Acid-catalyzed dehydration of glycerol removes water and generates the alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde acrolein.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative upstream feeder. The curated review notes, in the context of the Patel et al. (2015) cyanosulfidic framework, that acrolein can arise from thermal decomposition of glycerol and then feed 3-aminopropanal formation. Acidic mineral surfaces and low-water-activity drying phases make the dehydration chemically plausible, but this step was not experimentally established as part of the Patel et al. (2015) proline sequence.

reactions.name: Ammonia addition to acrolein

conditions.other: ammonia-rich evaporitic pool or shoreline film

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia performs conjugate addition to acrolein, followed by proton transfer and tautomerization to furnish 3-aminopropanal.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative upstream feeder. The curated review explicitly identifies acrolein plus NH3, via Michael-type addition, as a plausible source of 3-aminopropanal for the proline network. It is included because it gives the exact C3 amino aldehyde required by Patel et al. (2015), but the review also highlights the uncertain availability and stability of 3-aminopropanal in prebiotic pools.

reactions.name: Net reductive amination of malondialdehyde

conditions.other: warm sulfidic pool; overall net transformation with reduction supplied by the local geochemical redox environment

reactions.mechanism: One aldehyde of malondialdehyde forms an imine with ammonia, then surface-mediated reduction and proton transfer collapse the dialdehyde to the beta-amino aldehyde 3-aminopropanal.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative upstream feeder. The curated review also identifies reductive amination of malondialdehyde as a plausible source of 3-aminopropanal. FeS/NiS-type reducing surfaces make the net transformation chemically credible, but no direct experimental demonstration was provided in the curated report, and the same 3-aminopropanal stability problem remains (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cyanohydrin formation from 3-aminopropanal
reactions.mechanism: Cyanide adds to the aldehyde carbonyl of 3-aminopropanal, generating the alpha-hydroxynitrile 4-amino-2-hydroxybutanenitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Directly supported by the cyanosulfidic proline sequence of Patel et al. (2015). Cyanohydrin formation is the key C-C bond-forming step that converts the C3 amino aldehyde into the C4 aminonitrile needed for subsequent ring closure.

reactions.name: H2S-mediated thiolation-cyclization

conditions.other: sulfidic atmosphere or dissolved HS- in a cyanosulfidic pool

reactions.mechanism: HS- adds to the nitrile carbon to form a thioamide, then the terminal amine attacks intramolecularly to close a five-membered ring and release ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Directly supported by Patel et al. (2015). This H2S-mediated thiolation-cyclization is the proline-specific ring-forming step; the three-carbon tether in 3-aminopropanal gives the correct geometry for five-membered-ring closure. The review notes that real-world H2S recycling efficiency could limit turnover.

reactions.name: Cu/H2S reductive deoxygenation

conditions.other: cyanosulfidic pool with native copper precipitates

reactions.mechanism: Reductive deoxygenation removes the C3 hydroxyl group from the thione-bearing ring, producing pyrrolidine-2-thione and water.
reactions.reasoning: Directly supported by Patel et al. (2015), which used a Cu0/H2S reducing system to remove the C3 hydroxyl group. Native copper is geochemically plausible in sulfidic surface settings, but the review explicitly identifies sustained Cu0 availability on early Earth as an uncertainty.

reactions.name: Thione-to-nitrile exchange
reactions.mechanism: HCN attacks the thioamide carbon of pyrrolidine-2-thione; sulfur is displaced and a nitrile is installed at C2, regenerating H2S.
reactions.reasoning: Directly supported by Patel et al. (2015). Thione-to-nitrile exchange converts the sulfur heterocycle into the immediate nitrile precursor of proline and regenerates H2S, embedding the route in a sulfur-recycling loop.

reactions.name: Nitrile hydration to prolinamide

conditions.other: warm aqueous pool with prolonged residence time

reactions.mechanism: Water adds to the nitrile carbon to give an imidate or amide sequence, yielding pyrrolidine-2-carboxamide.
reactions.reasoning: Mechanistically justified subdivision of Patel et al. (2015) step 5. The curated review describes nitrile hydrolysis as proceeding through a carboxamide intermediate, so this node makes the first hydration event explicit. It is a mechanistic expansion rather than a separately validated standalone prebiotic route.

reactions.name: Amide hydrolysis to rac-proline

conditions.other: geothermal cycling or mild heating in surface pools

reactions.mechanism: Hydrolysis of the carboxamide releases ammonia and furnishes pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid as a racemate.
reactions.reasoning: Mechanistically justified completion of Patel et al. (2015) step 5. Hydrolysis of the amide yields rac-proline, but the review flags nitrile-derived hydrolysis chemistry as potentially slow under ambient conditions, making this a plausible bottleneck.

reactions.name: Net nitrile hydrolysis to rac-proline

conditions.other: one-pot hydrolysis in warm mineral-rich pools; amide does not accumulate detectably

reactions.mechanism: Overall nitrile hydrolysis proceeds through transient amide formation and collapse to rac-proline without isolable buildup of the amide node.
reactions.reasoning: Alternative net representation of Patel et al. (2015) step 5. The chemistry still proceeds through transient amide formation, but in warmer mineral-rich pools the amide need not accumulate to detectable levels. Because the review identifies hydrolysis kinetics and metal-ion catalysis as open questions, this branch is plausible but less resolved than the core cyanosulfidic steps.

reactions.name: Chiral mineral surface L-enrichment of proline

conditions.other: adsorption and desorption cycles at mineral interfaces in concentrated prebiotic pools

reactions.mechanism: Differential adsorption or desorption of enantiomers on chiral surface sites leaves an L-enriched dissolved proline pool.
reactions.reasoning: Explicitly speculative. The curated review states that Patel et al. (2015) chemistry gives racemic proline and mentions chiral mineral surfaces as one possible route to homochirality. This node therefore represents post-synthetic L-enrichment at mineral interfaces rather than a demonstrated asymmetric synthesis.

reactions.name: Asymmetric crystallization L-enrichment of proline

conditions.other: evaporation, freeze-thaw, or dissolution-recrystallization cycles in concentrated prebiotic pools

reactions.mechanism: A slight stochastic enantiomeric excess is amplified by preferential crystallization or eutectic partitioning, enriching L-proline relative to D-proline.
reactions.reasoning: Explicitly speculative. The review also mentions asymmetric crystallization as a possible origin of amino-acid enantioenrichment. This node models evaporation or freeze-thaw driven preferential crystallization leading to an L-enriched pool, but no proline-specific experimental support was provided in the curated report (Patel et al., 2015).

pathways.name: Direct acrolein feeder with stepwise hydrolysis and mineral L-enrichment
pathways.description: Acrolein is aminated to 3-aminopropanal, then follows the Patel cyanosulfidic ring-building sequence, stepwise nitrile hydrolysis through prolinamide, and post-synthetic L-enrichment at a biochemical mineral interface.

pathways.name: Direct acrolein feeder with stepwise hydrolysis and crystallization L-enrichment
pathways.description: The same acrolein-fed cyanosulfidic core is followed by explicit amide formation and hydrolysis, then by asymmetric crystallization to an L-enriched proline pool.

pathways.name: Direct acrolein feeder with net hydrolysis and mineral L-enrichment
pathways.description: Acrolein enters the core cyanosulfidic sequence, and the proline nitrile is hydrolyzed in one pot before chiral mineral-interface enrichment.

pathways.name: Direct acrolein feeder with net hydrolysis and crystallization L-enrichment
pathways.description: Acrolein feeds the same ring-forming core, but the nitrile hydrolysis is treated as a one-pot conversion before crystallization-driven L-enrichment.

pathways.name: Glycerol dehydration feeder with stepwise hydrolysis and mineral L-enrichment
pathways.description: A speculative glycerol-to-acrolein feeder supplies the core Patel sequence; proline nitrile is hydrolyzed through prolinamide, then L-enriched on chiral mineral interfaces.

pathways.name: Glycerol dehydration feeder with stepwise hydrolysis and crystallization L-enrichment
pathways.description: Glycerol first dehydrates to acrolein, then enters the cyanosulfidic ring-building route and explicit amide hydrolysis branch before asymmetric crystallization.

pathways.name: Glycerol dehydration feeder with net hydrolysis and mineral L-enrichment
pathways.description: Glycerol is dehydrated to acrolein, the core surface cyanosulfidic sequence builds the pyrrolidine framework, and one-pot nitrile hydrolysis is followed by mineral-interface L-enrichment.

pathways.name: Malondialdehyde feeder with stepwise hydrolysis and mineral L-enrichment
pathways.description: A speculative malondialdehyde-to-3-aminopropanal feeder enters the experimentally anchored cyanosulfidic core, then proceeds through prolinamide and mineral-interface L-enrichment.

pathways.name: Malondialdehyde feeder with stepwise hydrolysis and crystallization L-enrichment
pathways.description: Malondialdehyde feeds 3-aminopropanal by net reductive amination, after which the surface cyanosulfidic core and explicit amide hydrolysis branch deliver rac-proline for crystallization-based L-enrichment.

pathways.name: Malondialdehyde feeder with net hydrolysis and mineral L-enrichment
pathways.description: Malondialdehyde enters through net reductive amination to 3-aminopropanal; the cyanosulfidic core constructs the pyrrolidine framework, then one-pot nitrile hydrolysis and mineral-interface partitioning furnish an L-enriched product pool.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is a well-connected, literature-aligned route to DL-proline via direct acrolein amination and the Patel core sequence. However rxn_006 is unbalanced and needs an H2-equivalent or explicit reducing equivalents, rxn_007 is also unbalanced and needs an added H source/reducing equivalent, and rxn_011 is a speculative mineral-surface resolution rather than a demonstrated synthesis of L-proline.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_006 with explicit reducing equivalents; a balanced net form needs an added H2-equivalent alongside the Cu0/H2S system.
Correct rxn_007 to a fully balanced exchange with an explicit H source or reductant rather than the current H-deficient shorthand.
Either provide proline-specific evidence for rxn_011 on a named chiral mineral or stop the pathway at DL-proline.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Among the listed options this is the strongest overall: the acrolein feeder is plausible and the stepwise hydrolysis explicitly tracks the amide intermediate known for nitrile hydrolysis. It still falls short of approval because rxn_006 and rxn_007 violate conservation as encoded, and rxn_012 is only a speculative post-synthetic crystallization-based L-enrichment.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_006 with explicit reducing equivalents; the current encoding omits the H2-equivalent required by balance.
Correct rxn_007 stoichiometry and specify the full reagent set for thione-to-nitrile exchange.
Place rxn_012 in a defined evaporitic or wet-dry crystallization setting and support that rac-proline can actually enrich to L under those conditions.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The direct feeder and Patel core remain plausible, but the net hydrolysis shorthand in rxn_010 must be corrected to consume 2 H2O. Together with the unbalanced rxn_006 and rxn_007 and speculative rxn_011, this pathway is stronger for DL-proline than for L-proline.
suggestions: Repair rxn_006 and rxn_007 with explicit H-balance and redox bookkeeping.
Correct rxn_010 to mol_012 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_014 + mol_004.
Treat rxn_011 as a speculative resolution step unless proline-specific evidence is provided.

suggestions: Repair rxn_006 and rxn_007 with explicit H-balance and redox bookkeeping.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The downstream proline-forming chemistry is literature-grounded, but the glycerol feeder is underconditioned: rxn_001 should be glycerol -> acrolein + 2 H2O and likely needs hot acidic or mineral-catalyzed surface conditions. Combined with the unbalanced rxn_006 and rxn_007 and speculative rxn_011, confidence is only moderate.
suggestions: Correct rxn_001 to glycerol -> acrolein + 2 H2O and specify hot acidic or mineral-catalyzed surface conditions.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the better of the glycerol routes because crystallization-based enrichment is somewhat more concrete than unspecified mineral chirality, but the same feeder and core encoding issues remain. rxn_001 needs 2 H2O and stronger environmental justification, while rxn_006 and rxn_007 remain conservation violations.
suggestions: Correct rxn_001 to glycerol -> acrolein + 2 H2O and describe a realistic heated surface setting for it.
Repair rxn_006 and rxn_007 with explicit reducing equivalents.

suggestions: Correct rxn_001 to glycerol -> acrolein + 2 H2O and specify appropriate dehydration conditions.
Repair rxn_006 and rxn_007 with explicit H-balance and redox bookkeeping.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The Patel core from 3-aminopropanal onward is still reasonable, but the feeder is not: rxn_003 is UNBALANCED, lacks a reductant, and the supplied balance check only rescues it by implying O2 release, which is chemically implausible here. The unresolved mol_007 identifier further weakens this branch, and rxn_011 remains speculative.
suggestions: Replace rxn_003 with an explicitly balanced reductive amination that includes a defined reductant; as written the check only balances it by releasing O2.
Fix mol_007 with a valid structure identifier or InChI so the feeder can be validated.
Repair rxn_006 and rxn_007, and consider ending the branch at DL-proline unless a real enrichment mechanism is shown.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected network with enough nodes and strong literature alignment for the Patel et al. cyanosulfidic core from 3-aminopropanal to proline, and the narrative appropriately acknowledges uncertainty in chirality and aminoaldehyde availability. Network validity is only moderate because 7 of 12 reactions are balanced as written, rxn_001 and rxn_010 need coefficients, and rxn_003, rxn_006, and rxn_007 are UNBALANCED by the supplied check. To correct them: rxn_001 should be mol_006 -> mol_005 + 2 mol_003; rxn_003 needs an explicit reductant and oxygen fate rather than the implied O2 release; rxn_006 needs an added H2-equivalent with the Cu0/H2S reduction; rxn_007 also needs an added H source or reducing equivalent; rxn_010 should be mol_012 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_014 + mol_004. Environmental consistency is good for the surface cyanosulfidic core, weaker for glycerol dehydration and for labeling mineral adsorption or crystallization as Biochemical without a transfer scenario. The network clearly supports DL-proline formation better than L-proline: mol_015 is not stereochemically encoded beyond its label, and rxn_011 and rxn_012 are speculative post-synthetic enrichment steps rather than demonstrated prebiotic syntheses. mol_007 also has an unresolved identifier or InChI issue. Best supported pathway: P2, but the network is still below approval.
